A game with disgustingly overpriced microtransactions, an extremely dull and soulless feel the the game - it feels like I'm playing something made by AI even though it apparently isn't. Ugly looking graphics that appear as if the game was 1-2 generations ago in age, yet surprisingly is somehow extremely poorly optimized. Games are not really fun, they're a cheap way to waste time in the same way scrolling for hours is. I personally need to be under the influence of high doses of caffeine in order to get any enjoyment out of it. Questionable character designs - while some are quite comic accurate, many of the original ones make the characters appear interchangeable and they all lack their unique touch. Incredibly poor balance, do they even think their decisions through? The match-making is so bad that it's funny, and I don't really care much for the PVP aspect because of it. The community? Well, it is what you make of it. The developers can't necessarily help who plays their game and who doesn't, so the incredibly degenerate and often times toxic community isn't really a fair criticism about the game on the developers' side - and it isn't all toxic. You can very much meet and befriend people. 

Really what should've been made was a Marvel Ultimate Alliance 4 for a Marvel experience. Not this hollow shell of a title.

Note: I am a console player. My criticisms are about the game as a whole.

claims.claim: The user interface and menu system are described as confusing, difficult to navigate, and poorly designed.

citations.review_text: I gave this game about 15 seconds. And 15 seconds is too long!! Actually, I couldn't give this game 15 seconds, because the game was never a game. It was just a bunch of menus. No gameplay. I'll explain. First, it couldn't even run correctly. Had to install bits and bobs in Windows. Then it kept wanting elevation in Windows just to run at all. Then Steam Big Picture would get ejected. Then when I got in to finally load, it wanted me to enter a username. Every name was taken. I immediately alt+F4 to ask for a refund. Unacceptable! But then I realized I bought this game in 2024. I got confused with some other recent Steam purchases. So I tried it again. Put in something like "jkhfksjhfskjfhgdsiuhfs" as my username. Surprisingly it wasn't taken! Then I tried to play the game. The menus were atrocious. Some of the menus were just to check out characters. I couldn't care less. Just have one giant play button and let me play. I don't want to have to figure out your bad programming just to find my way around. Even when I did try to play, then it wanted to render shaders for who knows how long. It was at 30ish percent for entirely too long. And I have a badder PC than your mom, so it wasn't my PC. Then I told it who cares, just play, I don't care if the shaders aren't rendered, even though it warned me against doing it. Then there was a timer ticking up like I had to wait on people to join to play? I have no idea. Anything beyond 15 seconds to play a game, and start it up, and progress towards fun and action and gameplay is unacceptable. Thanks for nothing. If you can still refund me, shoot me an email. Yay refunds! :)

[h1]You play with bots in matchmaking when matching to fight REAL HUMANS!![/h1]

Played on release and one massive complain with matchmaking was that if you lost a match you'd end up in a bot match right after, it was annoying then and unfortunately it's still an issue, no idea if it gets better after a while but it is incredibly painful going from a match where you basically learn nothing into a match where the enemy team is locked in while your team is eating crayons.

This kind of matchmaking is absolutely horrible especially since there is no way around this, you either play quick play, comp (which is locked until you're lvl 15 so enjoy quick play until then lmao) or wacky arcade modes (PvE is good, wish it was more in depth during the gameplay part). It's more annoying at the start when you're getting to unlock comp because until then you're stuck in this circle of bot matches and getting stomped because half your team refuses to put in more effort than needed to fight bots in real matches.

Another really big issue is because communication is non-existent; the game will never really showcase who is swapping to who which since there is ONLY OPEN QUEUE IN QUICK PLAY which isn't a bad thing on its own it is extremely bad when the game doesn't communicate well enough when your ONE TANK/SUPPORT swaps to DPS and goes 0/10.

I get it it's a F2P casual game and people just wanna play with their favourite heroes and all but hotdog this hurts the matchmaking so bad...

If they'd only fix this ONE massive annoying part of playing vs bots in the PLAYER VS PLAYER QUEUE it'd beat overwatch easily until then.. actually i'm not holding hopes they had 2 years to fix this.
Very bad matchmaking: you stomp or get stomped, nothing fair in between. However, really cool summer skins for male and female characters.

This is probably the worst game Ive ever played in my life. The developers refuse to fix their lopsided matchmaking so I honestly just stopped playing. Its not fun knowing that after you win a certain amount of times the games matchmaking system is going to force you to lose. This game is like going to the casino and playing a slot machine. Its just luck whether you win or lose atp. Making the ranked gameplay a endless loop of winning games with teammates of your caliber, to then being put on teams with teammates with a history of throwing and abandoning games, and just not being good at all in general. Its like they're basically playing with your emotions like a drug to keep you hooked in hopes that your next game " you finally have good teammates" by then you've lost like 8 games in a row. Its disgusting and im glad im not playing this game anymore

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from performance and optimization issues, with some noting high memory usage, storage space requirements, and frame rate drops.

citations.review_text:
Despite my decent specs I cannot run this game (I am talking 0 frames mostly to 16 frames) because for some reason it keeps trying to use my integrated graphics card instead of my main one. I had to fix this in esoteric NVIDIA settings that were very hard to find and took much online searching, yet it still ran poorly due to how poorly optimized this game is. On lowest everything settings. It takes up so much RAM and the shaders have to download all the time. The game has been out since 2024, yet it still doesn't run on my specs which is a $1000 USD PC. And all my drivers are up to date. I made sure to close all background stuff too.
I can run all other shooters perfectly fine, such as Battlefield 6, this is literally the only game I have tried that gives me issues to the point I can't run it on lowest everything settings.
Oh, and after "fixing" it, my settings reset again for no reason so it's back to using my integrated graphics card (I saw the game stated as using my integrated card in NVIDIA settings, but it's a very common issue) instead of my main one again (see attached specs).
Is it so hard to fix this? Why does no other shooter or game I know of do this? You had nearly 2 years now. I wanted to like this game and would have played it a fair amount otherwise.
This game runs on 40-50 fps on my pc, I'm Greatful but respectfully this game was kind of trash. Deadpool is the only reason to play this game in my opinion and this game takes a lot STORAGE.

Why does the freaking menu use 4GB+ memory??
It's borderline unplayable with 16GB of RAM..

I remember loving this game during the early days and playtest back when it was like 20-40gb. 
While my pc did struggle with the game i could still totally play it without many issues. Now due to the game being well over 80gb i just does not feel worth it to play anymore. Especially with my limited 250gb games drive (I have a sperate 250gb  one for my os and like everything else). I really hope that the rivals devs put some more effort into optimizing their game on pc especially when the game is now on PS4.
its fun but requires  a lot of ram (recommended at least 16 gbs) also  takes a lot of times to get good with specific characters

Theres also a small amount of people that use config mods just to be able to run the game better on lower end PC's, because even setting everything to LOW, Is just not enough, but rather than fixing or even mitigate these Issues, they'd rather ban configs as a whole.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game's visuals as cluttered and chaotic, making it difficult to track abilities and understand what is happening during fights.

citations.review_text:
[b]Marvel Rivals is what happens when chaos gets a Marvel license and decides to become a personality test.[/b]

One match you are a god.
Next match you are a spectator watching a glowing fever dream erase your sanity.

[i]The game is loud.
The game is flashy.
The game is unreasonably committed to making every fight look like a trailer.[/i]

People say it is unbalanced.
People say it is too much.
People say it is pure visual nonsense.

And they are right.

That is exactly why it works.

You queue up for fun and leave with:
- damaged ego,
- a clip you will replay for a week,
- and at least one teammate you now consider a personal enemy.

The awards should have a category called:
[b]“Most Likely To Trigger A Group Chat.”[/b]
Marvel Rivals wins that.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that matchmaking produces heavily lopsided matches, described as being stomps or heavily unbalanced regarding player levels and skill gaps.

citations.review_text:
The matchmaking system feels rigged. After going on a 3-match win streak, I was immediately hit with a 6-match losing streak. It often feels like the game deliberately puts you into unwinnable matches just to force your win rate back down.

If you're okay with a matchmaking system that feels manipulated, then go ahead and play. Otherwise, I'd recommend staying away.

On top of that, team cooperation is terrible. Everyone wants to play Duelist, while almost no one is willing to pick Vanguard or Strategist. This leads to poorly balanced team compositions and frustrating matches.

Overall, the game feels heavily unbalanced, and the matchmaking only makes the experience worse.

and dive need more counters, casuals such as myself am not having fun when i met dive after dive after dive, and my teammate just refuse to change hero to counter them. why? because they're level 50 below and maybe they're knowledge on the game is not that much yet. and i'm the only one that always change to the thing, namor, and whatnot, making me unable to use the other heros that i want to give a shot. pretty much locking me into the peel guy.  and if i'm want to try the other 80% of the heroes that  are duelists our team ended with no tanks. great matchmaking guys!!.

it has an "e sports" btw, and they're been pushing e sports over and over again, but you never seen anyone talking about it, probably becuase how unbalanced the characters in this game is.

"Just heal each other," they say, charging headfirst into the enemy while both healers are busy keeping one another alive. Somehow, it's still the healers' fault.

I'm leaving a negative review because of the game's balance. The developers have consistently balanced around DPS perspectives while neglecting strategists/healers, leaving those roles with far less agency and, in my opinion, the least respect.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the matchmaking and ranked system as severely flawed, resulting in matches that feel like one-sided blowouts and pairing skilled players with uncoordinated teammates.

citations.review_text: Marvel Rivals is a game with a good vision, but several integral flaws deliberately build in to the experience. We live in an era where people are immensely prideful because corporations have learned that human nature is quite profitable. To ensure that everybody keeps buying their goonbait cosmetics, NetEase feels very strongly about artificially keeping all players around a 50% win rate via the complex, hidden MMR-based matchmaking system. Unfortunately, the match-making is quite overtuned, as a player with a high MMR stat for a particular rank will be matched with the lowest MMR players available. The game does not feel competitive whatsoever. Either you're walking the enemy team or you're being walked. Very rarely are there competitive matches, and that's before taking into account players that leave games or grief lobbies to sabotage matches. Griefers exist in every game, but the responsibility and blame falls upon NetEase because they do not sufficiently punish this behavior in ranked. As I was saying, not only are most player kept between a 45%-55% win rate by design, but the system is designed to reward points in ranked based off of your hidden MMR stat compared to the average hidden MMR stat of the enemy team. As you gain rank, personal performance is an unimportant factor. What this means is that a player who is good at the game will have to put much more effort in to win games, since they have bad players on their team. The inverse is true. This also means that when fighting a team of a standard MMR, a player with high MMR loses more points on a loss and gains fewer points on a win than the players that he or she carried to the win. It is easier to rank up in this game if you are not good at it. It is the inverse of competitive. The rank distribution alone can explain why this is a problem. You'd think that if you were in Celestial II, you'd be able to have competent teammates, but you're likely going to match with players that should be in Diamond if you…

The game used to be so fun in the beginning but having a new hero every month quickly killed the game. Every now and then there are buffed heroes no one asked for. In most of games there are the same 10-15 heroes, while the rest are unplayable against meta team comps. Tank role is pure torture, everyone picks DPS characters, healing in this game is ridiculous. 
Not to mention the eatarded matchmaking system that puts in such horrendous teams. You'll never have gradual progress to the next rank - instead EOMM will put you against a team of smurfs whereas yours seems mentally challenged. Playing ranked will absolutely drain you mentally, making you not feeling anything even after a win. 
Devs are too busy creating a million more gooner skins for the consumer-community buying the coins and battle passes instead of fixing the balance issues and matchmaking. 

It's sad to admit but this game is indeed dying; faster than overwatch 1 did. You can try playing quickplay mode and have some fun for some time but the joy of first months after the release is gone. Terrible updates, broken heroes and zero balance, horrible player-base turned this gem into a bin full of garbage and some shiny skins. Would not recommend to anyone.

The season 9 rework has unfortunately broken this game. I was excited but hestitant when they first announced these changes because I felt it was going to be a balancing nightmare, and it is. the game has turned from thoughtful use of abilities and managing cooldowns, to an ability spamming blurry nightmare. It has suffered massively competitively, the new team-up abilities added range from "near useless" to "I'm now ridiculously overpowered for the next 15 seconds because I pushed one button". It's an unbelievable mess to play right now, and i think once the excitement of these changes wears off people are gonna see that it's very damaging to the long term health of the game. I am a consistent celestial rank player and as such I feel I have a pretty decent understanding of the flow and mechanics of the game, but that flow has turned from a decently good balance of evenly matched players and teamfights, to roll or get rolled, I have seldom seen a neck and neck game in this new update. Some heroes also now lack definitive counters, for example Hela's ultimate, before this update she ascended into the sky, gained a bunch of health and shot high damage blasts at the ground, theres a few ways to counter this, A) pretty much any healer ult. B) strange shield or mag shield does a pretty decent job at absorbing hits from yourself and your team. C) run away or hide behind indestructible objects. D) focus fire her until her ult health was depleted. Those are all good options and they all show atleast a bit of consistency, however, that ult that could previously two-tap "squishy" hero's, can now additonally spawn squids on every shot that have their own health pool and also do absurds amount of damage, and because of the way this ability works means she can spawn them in any direction and anywhere within her line of site on the battlefield which makes shields and running away effectively useless. tanks can no longer protect their team from this ability as it attacks from all …

claims.claim: Reviewers report that recent game updates have drastically increased damage output and healing effectiveness, leading to unbalanced matches and an over-reliance on ability spam.

citations.review_text: This update is absolute crap!!! You take so much damage just by looking at an enemy. Plus, you can't kill anyone because everyone can heal now. What are you even thinking when you make updates like this? There are so many projectiles in a single battle that the game starts to lag. And they brought back the team ups that everyone hated so much. GREAT! Back up the update pls!

This game is in an unbelievable state right now, and perhaps the worst it's ever been in. This game is hyper overstimulation now constantly, and what was already a poorly balanced game is now absolutely way worse. I have played since beta, and this just sucks. There is infinite damage, infinite CCs, one shot combos, and just sheer imbalance.

Making everybody OP is not fun. This is no competitive environment, this is a meme, a chaos mode that somehow made the default mode.

Season 9 is easily the worst update Marvel Rivals has had. The game has gone from a hero shooter with unique identities, to an ability-spam slop where every fight is just ult spam, visual clutter, and team-up explosions.

Black Widow's rework is especially awful. They removed what made her unique...a high-skill precision sniper...and turned her into another generic DPS. Her identity is gone.

Instead of improving balance, the update made the game more chaotic, less strategic, and far less rewarding. I tried coming back to the game but these changes make the game unplayable for me...

Overstimulated!!! Ult spam, tanks don't die... Too much damage, too much healing... Balancing has left the chat!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that recent updates to the team-up system grant characters multiple new and overpowered abilities, destroying the game's balance and tactical depth.

citations.review_text:
I love Marvel Rivals. I have over 2,100 hours because I genuinely enjoyed playing it, but this update completely killed the fun for me.

It feels like the whole game is built around team-ups now. They're way too strong, and it honestly feels like almost anyone can get kills just by abusing them. The skill gap is disappearing. Good aim, movement, positioning, and actually being better at the game don't matter as much anymore when a team-up can do so much of the work.

A lot of my friends feel the same way. We used to play this game every day because it rewarded skill, but now it just feels frustrating. Every match turns into people spamming broken team-ups instead of actually outplaying each other.

I'm not saying remove team-ups completely, but they seriously need to be balanced. Right now they make the game feel less competitive and way less fun.

I really love this game, which is why this sucks so much. I just want Marvel Rivals to go back to rewarding skill instead of relying so heavily on team-ups. Please rebalance them or even roll back some of these changes. fast before this game dies like overwatch because of bad updates likes this.

(review written 11/07/26)
we are at a point with the new team up system where the game is almost unplayably unbalanced. the entire downside of teamups is that if you wanted a busted teamup, you had to learn how to use a character that you may not be great at, or put time into learning a new hero. if we remove that then the entire cast of characters just gets two new abilities, which at this point in time seems like they are either ridiculously overpowered or unplayably bad. at this point tier lists are going to need an S+ tier because there are some characters that have literally ascended to godhood. they claim to have playtested the update intensively and yet some bugs about characters (like luna or bp) where luna literally can cleanse herself of CC (which is an ability that is locked to certain characters with a high opportunity cost) or have cooldowns so low you might as well have removed them. some of the old teamups which people complained incessantly about being broken (namor gamma squids, punisher infinite ammo) have NO DOWNSIDE ANYMORE, and you can just pick the character and get the teamup FOR FREE, and it seems like they have not been tuned in the slightest for the current meta, just copy-pasting the ability and calling it a day. visual clutter is at an all time high with EVERY character in the game having an extra ability and as a casual/ranked gold player trying to learn what everyone's new teamups do AND which ones are good AND how to counter them when most of them are so OP that you genuinely can't even move out of spawn, it just doesn't seem like a good use of my time.

tldr; game is borderline unplayable right now for both new players and old, especially casuals. wait until season 10, and if they don't fix it by then the game will probably be dead anyway

Season 9 was the death for the game for me. they reworked everything, I cant comprehend the amount of things happening at the same time now with over 100 new abilities. there is really no time to think and react in a smart way. It's just spam abilities with minimal thinking and maybe you will catch something that is broken for a specific composition. if it's it - it's it and you don't even know why it works or why the enemy just doesn't seem to have his hp decreased at all no matter what you do. i liked the game before season 9. i can't say i enjoyed season 8.5 so much, it was also bad. matchmaking got worse over time but the new rework completely ruined the experience for me. After 1.5 years of daily gameplay, I'm deeply disappointed and considering deleting and moving on.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the season 9 update as introducing excessive visual clutter and particle effects that make team fights difficult to read.

citations.review_text:
[h1]An Overwhelming, Chaotic Mess of a Season[/h1]

I love the core gameplay of Marvel Rivals, but the latest Season 9 update completely ruins the flow of the game. It feels like the developers tried to fix things that weren't broken, and instead, they just created a frustrating experience for casual and veteran players alike.

[b]The Main Issues:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Visual Pollution:[/b] Team fights are completely unreadable now. The updated team-up abilities and extra visual effects make the screen a blinding mess of flashing lights. You will die without even knowing what hit you.
[*] [b]Unnecessary Complexity:[/b] Upgrading every single hero with new mechanics has spiked the learning curve to an exhausting degree. What used to be a fun, strategic hero shooter now feels like a chore to keep up with.
[*] [b]Awful Balance & Meta:[/b] Healing feels completely useless against the new team-up setups. Matches either end in a total steamroll or drag out into tedious, unkillable brawls. 
[*] [b]Ranked is Broken:[/b] Matchmaking feels worse than ever this season, and the bugs are piling up.
[/list]

If you enjoyed the clean, tactical team play of earlier seasons, prepare to be disappointed. I cannot recommend playing this season.

The visual gore in this game, is horrendous. I came back to play season 9, after stopping around season 4. The sheer amount of screen clutter, AOE's, Beams, Highlights, indicators, for all abilities firing off so many times, makes it hard to focus. There is just too much clutter visually to be interested or focused on the game. 

Season 0-1 was a great launch, with some fab fresh feeling to the hero shooter market. But it's gotten so cluttered visually, that I cannot play this anymore, it isn't fun. Also, some of the balance changes to characters is insane, how are the healers, able to sustain so much damage against dive characters. Every ult that seems to come out, is an AOE shield heal, that no one can really die within. 

I hope they make some changes, but as of writing this, the game has gotten so messy both visually and balance wise, I cannot rec it in it's current state.

Season 9 has the be THE WORST f*cking update ive ever played. so much f*cking particles that you cant see sh*t, the damage output is too much even with a trip supp comp, it's kill or be killed. I wanted to like the changes but i only play this game on a casual basis. i am not that good and i play with friends, but even then, its incredibly difficult to even enjoy a qp game because i just end up in a loss after loss after f*cking loss. until this sh*tty update gets reverted, im done with this f*ck*ss game.

Let me clarify this with I have well over 2000 hours total on this game spread through multiple alts. 
I want to make it clear I think this game is GOOD, it's fun and very easy to get into.
However...
This negative review is specifically targeting the biggest issue the game has right now.
The amount of post FX/Effects in general going on in this game is genuinely too much. It's not slightly too much, it's just way too much. This is coming from someone who has gamed and played probably well over 10k hours on shooters since I was born easily. THERE IS WAY TOO MUCH VISUAL CLUTTER. This season actually ruined the game in my opinion in so many possible ways. The biggest way is by far the new team up system that literally just makes this chaotic and not in the good way. It is literally just too much happening at once. Please lower the amount of effects going on in general, dial it down at least 30-40% MINIMUM.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the community features rampant toxic behavior, including verbal abuse, griefing, and intentional throwing, with insufficient developer punishment.

citations.review_text: The game is ok, definitely a big pull for anyone that's a fan of the Marvel IP, but the rudeness is intolerable. I have to uninstall and stop playing for periods of time because players are abusive in both chat and voice, even in quickplay. There are settings to mute chat, but then the whole teamwork aspect goes downhill. Playing is not worth the verbal abuse that is rampant.

I've played Marvel Rivals since the beginning because I genuinely believed this game had the potential to become one of the best hero shooters on the market. The gameplay is fun, the heroes feel unique, and the Marvel universe is the perfect setting for this type of game. That's what makes it so disappointing to finally walk away.

The biggest reason I'm leaving isn't balance, matchmaking, or even the bugs. It's the community and the complete lack of meaningful action from the developers to improve it.

Nearly every session turns into dealing with players insulting each other, blaming teammates after the first lost fight, intentionally throwing matches, going AFK, or quitting altogether. It's become normal. Instead of looking forward to playing, I found myself wondering how many toxic teammates I'd have to deal with before I could actually enjoy a match.

People always say, "Just mute them," but that misses the point. Muting chat doesn't stop people from griefing, feeding, AFKing, or intentionally ruining games because they're angry. Toxicity is more than words, and that's where this game is failing.

The developers keep giving us new skins, new heroes, and balance updates, but none of that matters if the overall experience keeps getting worse. A live-service game lives or dies by its community, and right now Marvel Rivals feels like it's losing that battle. Reporting players rarely feels like it accomplishes anything, and because of that, toxic behavior keeps getting worse.

What frustrates me most is that the game itself is actually good. The combat is fun. The characters are fun. The potential is there. But every good match is buried under several miserable ones where someone decides to throw because they didn't get the hero they wanted or starts attacking their own teammates five minutes into the game.

Eventually, I realized I wasn't logging in because I was excited I was logging in hoping this time would be different. It almost never was.

I'm no…

At the time of writing this review, the game is in Season 9 of its run and it has never been more fun. I've played since launch and consistently tried to participate in the ranked ladder every season, with my highest being around Diamond 1. Every character feels meaningful (in spite of what a lot of dive enjoyers may tell you) and your competency with them is equally important to your game sense. It should, on paper, all feel great to play. So why doesn't it? 

Plain and simply, it's the community. No, not the "gooner" skins that puritans will cry to you about from their heightened pillars of morality, not the balance of particular heroes (which is already extremely subjective and boils down to what role you play the most and what issues it runs into), and certainly not the fact the game has no hard locked role queue. It is the fact that people are allowed to behave in abhorrent, childish ways, and not be penalized for it in the slightest. While it may come with the territory of this kind of game, and I do wholeheartedly agree that it's a given that there will always be slur-slinging slashers or salty andys that just rage out and make your match harder for it, they have been for a year now allowed to proliferate unabated by the Devs, continuing to be more blatant and bold in their poor behavior.

I understand that because of the very short content cycles we have they are already inundated with enough work as is, but sooner or later I hope we can stop giving people a slap on the wrist for their toxicity and actually start culling them, so we can create an actually fun environment for the people who do wants to play with others and work as a team. It won't ever be a utopia, not when part of the problem stems from the influencers who popularize the game and don't take into account how they can impress others, but when the resort to making matches tolerable is muting pings and chat completely (as I have) I believe it is a sign that we can do better. I'm not a developer,…

The biggest reason I'm leaving isn't balance, matchmaking, or even the bugs. It's the community and the complete lack of meaningful action from the developers to improve it.

Nearly every session turns into dealing with players insulting each other, blaming teammates after the first lost fight, intentionally throwing matches, going AFK, or quitting altogether. It's become normal. Instead of looking forward to playing, I found myself wondering how many toxic teammates I'd have to deal with before I could actually enjoy a match.

People always say, "Just mute them," but that misses the point. Muting chat doesn't stop people from griefing, feeding, AFKing, or intentionally ruining games because they're angry. Toxicity is more than words, and that's where this game is failing.

The developers keep giving us new skins, new heroes, and balance updates, but none of that matters if the overall experience keeps getting worse. A live-service game lives or dies by its community, and right now Marvel Rivals feels like it's losing that battle. Reporting players rarely feels like it accomplishes anything, and because of that, toxic behavior keeps getting worse.

What frustrates me most is that the game itself is actually good. The combat is fun. The characters are fun. The potential is there. But every good match is buried under several miserable ones where someone decides to throw because they didn't get the hero they wanted or starts attacking their own teammates five minutes into the game.

Eventually, I realized I wasn't logging in because I was excited I was logging in hoping this time would be different. It almost never was.
